A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RouteFinder and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Content can be matched across relocation and renumbering, including Appendices A–D in both versions and the added Appendix E in v4.

before.justification: V3 reports original RouteFinder benchmark results, component ablations, generalization experiments and EAL finetuning results in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V4 retains those original empirical results and additionally displays individual routing solutions and their objective values in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Appendix B.2 revises the stated SwiGLU feed-forward computation in Equation (16) to a three-matrix gated MLP. This is a localized model-specification revision; the environment, MBT, reward normalization and EAL procedures remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that the implementation or trained models changed.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same 48 VRP variants, synthetic benchmarks, out-of-distribution attribute settings and CVRPLIB instances. Appendix E visualizes existing Table 1 test instances. The capacity-generalization experiment moves from v3 Appendix D.1 to v4 Section 5.1.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain HGS-PyVRP, OR-Tools, MTPOMO, MVMoE, single-variant POMO models, AL and training from scratch, including the additional CVRPLIB comparators. Appendix E illustrates neural methods already evaluated in Table 1.

E3.justification: Training remains 300 epochs with 100,000 instances per epoch and batch size 256. Evaluation retains greedy multistarts and eight symmetric augmentations; finetuning remains 10 epochs with 10,000 instances per epoch. Data-generation rules, hyperparameters and generalization settings match.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds qualitative case comparisons showing individual solutions across five neural models for the 16 main benchmark variants. Existing component ablations, MBT stability and imbalance studies, t-SNE analyses and generalization studies are retained; several are simply promoted into the main text.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies independent-run or seed counts. V4 adds no confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures. The existing training-variability plots are reused.

E6.justification: All corresponding benchmark and finetuning tables retain their numerical entries. New Figures 15–16 report individual solutions and objective values, such as CVRP costs of 14.868 for MTPOMO and 14.806 for RF-TE. These are newly displayed cases, not changes in aggregate performance.

T1.justification: Equation (16) replaces the sigmoid/bias/matrix-product expression with W3 applied to the Hadamard product of SiLU(W1x) and W2x, and revises the associated operator and parameter definitions. This is mathematically substantive. Other formal definitions and derivations remain unchanged, with no new proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same framework contributions, 48-variant scope, claimed performance advantages and adaptation to unseen attributes. The expanded main-text evidence does not introduce a new central contribution or broaden these claims.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations of MBT stability, global-embedding separation and EAL initialization advantages. The conclusion and Appendix C.3 preserve the tradeoff against single-variant models and the remaining performance gap to traditional solvers. Main-text elaborations largely repeat existing appendix interpretations.

D1.justification: A new Appendix B.2 footnote identifies the ParallelGatedMLP implementation and its StripedHyena inspiration. Section 5 expands the data-generation and evaluation description, largely summarizing details already in v3's appendices. Hardware, hyperparameters, code access and licensing remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds positioning relative to learned exact solvers, citing Gasse et al. and Prouvost et al., and adds references including Neural Deconstruction Search. Appendix B.2 adds SiLU and StripedHyena references, while the Sutton et al. citation is removed. Most other bibliographic changes update existing works.

P1.justification: V4 clarifies the MBT explanation and reorganizes Section 5 with explicit data-generation, generalization and MBT discussions drawn partly from the appendices. Appendix D.7 gains clearer subheadings, and the generic Impact Statement is removed. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column TMLR layout. Evidence is extensively rearranged: v3 Table 6 becomes v4 Table 2, v3 Figure 9 joins v4 Figure 4, and v3 Figure 14 becomes v4 Figure 7. Selected MBT curves are redisplayed, and Figures 15–16 add extensive solution grids.

improvement.justification: V4 improves technical clarity through the revised SwiGLU specification and implementation note, and makes existing generalization and finetuning evidence easier to follow within Section 5. Appendix E provides concrete solution examples. These are useful, limited improvements; the central empirical evidence and scientific scope remain unchanged.
